query: Review otel-collector-agent.yaml. It is the DaemonSet agent config for our prod EKS cluster and we are about to roll it out everywhere. Tell me what breaks and what to change, with the corrected pipeline.
expected_behavior: Moves `memory_limiter` to the front of every processor list and states that the Collector does not enforce this: a config with memory_limiter last starts cleanly with no warning, so the misordering only shows up as an OOM under load, never as a startup error

Identifies the fatal one: the `otlp` receiver declares `grpc: {}` and `http: {}` with no `endpoint`, and the default is `localhost` (127.0.0.1:4317 / :4318), so a containerised agent binds to loopback and receives nothing from other pods - the endpoint must be set to 0.0.0.0 explicitly

Rejects `tail_sampling` on a DaemonSet agent: each agent only sees the spans produced on its own node, so a multi-node trace is split and every shard is decided on partial data. Tail sampling requires a gateway tier fed by a `load_balancing` exporter that hashes on trace ID, with a headless Service so DNS returns individual pod IPs

Flags `resource` upserting `service.name: eks-prod`, which overwrites the identity every SDK set and collapses every service in the cluster into one node in the service map; identity attributes should use `action: insert` (or be fixed at the SDK) while `k8s.cluster.name` is legitimately an `upsert`

Flags `pod_association` with only `from: connection`: behind a service mesh the Collector sees the sidecar proxy's IP, so enrichment silently attaches the wrong pod. `k8s.pod.uid` from the downward API must be the first source, with connection as fallback

Notes that `spanmetrics` is fed from the traces pipeline *after* `tail_sampling`, so the derived RED metrics are computed from 5% of traffic plus all errors - rate and error-rate come out wrong in opposite directions. Metrics must be materialised from spans before any sampling step

Flags `user.id` as a `spanmetrics` dimension as a cardinality bomb: every dimension multiplies the series count, and an unbounded user identifier belongs on the span or in an exemplar, never in a metric label

Points out that `memory_limiter.limit_mib` is compared against the Go heap, not process RSS, so the container memory limit has to sit meaningfully above 1024 MiB or the kernel OOM-kills the process before the limiter ever refuses data

Does not claim the unused declared components (`hostmetrics` in the traces case, `batch`, `debug`) make the Collector fail to start - `batch` is declared but referenced by no pipeline and the Collector accepts that; removing it is hygiene, and leaving the `debug` exporter on the production logs pipeline is the real finding because it prints every log record to stdout
Keeps the corrected config as OTel Collector YAML and does not answer with CloudWatch, Azure Monitor or Cloud Logging product configuration

query: checkout-telemetry.ts is our OpenTelemetry setup. Production traces are useless - we can never find the request a customer complains about, and the dashboards disagree with each other. Fix the instrumentation.
expected_behavior: Removes `TraceIdRatioBasedSampler(0.05)` from the SDK and leaves the default AlwaysOn sampler, because a head-sampling decision is made before the request's outcome is known, so the 5% dice roll throws away exactly the error and latency outliers being looked for; sampling belongs in the Collector where tail policies can see the finished trace

Replaces the interpolated span names (`POST /api/orders/${orderId}/pay`, `charge_provider_${orderId}`, `expire_cart_${row.id}`) with low-cardinality names derived from the route template - `POST /api/orders/:orderId/pay` - and moves the identifier to an attribute

Corrects the span status rules per span kind: a 400 on the SERVER span is not an error because the server answered a bad request correctly and should be left UNSET, while the CLIENT span to the payment provider must be ERROR on 4xx and 5xx instead of the unconditional `OK` it sets today, and `OK` should only be set on confirmed success rather than speculatively

Migrates the deprecated attribute names to the stable HTTP conventions - `http.method` to `http.request.method`, `http.status_code` to `http.response.status_code`, `http.url` to `url.full` - and explains that instrumentation libraries gate this behind the `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` environment variable, where `http` switches to the stable set and `http/dup` emits both for a phased migration (`/dup` wins if both values are present)

Replaces `span.recordException(err)` with an exception log record emitted inside the active span context, carrying `exception.type`, `exception.message` and `exception.stacktrace` plus the span's `trace_id`/`span_id`, because the Span Event API is on a deprecation path in favour of log-based events

Replaces `console.log` with a structured logger emitting a stable event name and machine-readable fields, and requires `trace_id`/`span_id` on every record so a log line can be pivoted to its trace - this is what makes 'find the request this customer complained about' possible at all

Fixes the metric label sets: `user_id`, `order_id`, `error_message` and the raw `path` are unbounded and must come off `payment_attempts` and `checkout_latency`, leaving a bounded set such as route template, provider and status class; the identifiers move to spans, logs or exemplars
Notes that `checkout_latency` is a histogram, so every label multiplies by roughly the bucket count plus three - trimming labels on a histogram is worth an order of magnitude more than on a counter

Wraps `reconcileAbandonedCarts` in an explicit root span of kind SERVER or INTERNAL, because a headless job with no inbound request leaves the first auto-instrumented call as a parentless CLIENT root span, and collapses the per-row spans into one batch span with a `batch.size` attribute rather than one span per cart
Adds a graceful shutdown that calls `sdk.shutdown()` on SIGTERM, since the SDK batches before export and an unflushed process exit loses the spans from the request that caused the crash

query: Our checkout on-call gets about 40 pages a week and almost all of them get acked with no action. Here are the alert rules and the SLO definition. Rebuild this so the pager means something.
expected_behavior: Demotes `HighCPU`, `MemoryPressure`, `PodRestarted` and `DiskFilling` from page to dashboard or ticket because they alert on causes rather than on something a user feels, and keeps paging only for symptoms - failed checkouts and slow checkouts

Replaces the count-based `ErrorCount` (`increase(...) > 100` over 5m) with a ratio, since an absolute count fires on a busy afternoon when nothing is wrong and stays silent during a traffic drop when everything is

Rejects `SLOBreached` as structurally unable to page in time: a 30-day window means the alert only fires once the budget is already gone, and with a 30-day averaging window it then stays firing for weeks. Replaces it with multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts - a fast burn (roughly 14.4x over a 1h long window paired with a 5m short window, consuming ~2% of the budget) that pages, and a slower burn (about 6x over 6h, and 1x-3x over a day or more) that tickets
Explains the short-window requirement: the second, shorter window exists so the alert resolves promptly once the burn stops, instead of staying latched for the length of the long window

Calls 99.99% over 30 days an unjustified target - about 4 minutes 22 seconds of allowed failure per month, so a single pod rollout or one bad deploy exhausts it - and recommends dropping to 99.9% (roughly 43 minutes) unless the business genuinely requires otherwise

Fixes the latency SLI: `avg(rate(sum)/rate(count))` is an average, not the p95 the file claims, and an average hides the tail that the SLO exists to protect. Replaces it with a good-events ratio - the fraction of requests whose histogram bucket is under the latency threshold, via `histogram_quantile` on the bucket series or a threshold-bucket count
Points out the availability SLI counts every non-5xx as good, which credits 4xx storms, timeouts and any request that never produced a status code as successes

Flags both recording rules as silently corrupt: `rate(sum without (pod, instance) (http_requests_total)[5m:30s])` sums a counter across pods *before* taking the rate, so the independent counter resets of different pods interleave on the summed series and every pod restart reads as a reset - the aggregation has to happen after `rate()`, as `sum without (pod, instance) (rate(...[5m]))`, and the subquery form hides the defect behind valid-looking syntax

Catches the `ProviderLatency` unit error: `http_client_request_duration_seconds_bucket` is in seconds because the stable OpenTelemetry HTTP conventions renamed `http.client.duration` to `http.client.request.duration` and changed its unit from milliseconds to seconds, so a threshold of `> 800` ported from the old metric now means 800 seconds and the alert can never fire. The fix is `> 0.8`, and the general rule is that a rename which also changes a unit invalidates every threshold derived from the old metric

Notes that the same semantic-convention migration is what an instrumentation library gates behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`, where `<category>` switches to the stable names and `<category>/dup` emits both for a phased rollout (`/dup` taking precedence when both are set), so during a dual-emit window two metric names with different units coexist and an alert must name which one it is reading
Requires each surviving paging alert to carry a `for:` duration and a runbook link, and collapses severity to two tiers (page now / ticket this week) rather than adding more levels
Sets an error-budget policy with a consequence - freeze risky changes when the budget is spent - instead of 'discuss in the weekly platform meeting'

query: Read prod-incident-signals.md. This is everything we have from last week's checkout incident - it never reproduced locally or in staging. Work out what happened and tell me what to change so next time the signals actually answer the question.
expected_behavior: Names the `labeldrop` of `pod`, `instance`, `user_id` and `order_id` as the cause of the absurd `rate()` values: collapsing distinct series merges their independent counter resets and lands multiple samples on one series per scrape, so rate explodes and samples-per-minute go up rather than down - and the damage is silent, with no config error and no evidence left in the data

States the only safe scrape-time action is dropping an entire metric by `__name__`, and that reducing the cardinality of a label that makes a series unique has to happen at the source (template the path, stop emitting the identifier) or post-ingest with a counter-reset-aware aggregation, never with `labeldrop`

Reads the `status/tsdb` output correctly: `checkout_latency_bucket` at 2.8M series is a histogram, so its label cardinality is amplified by roughly the bucket count plus three, and `user_id` at 402k and `order_id` at 391k unique values are the labels that must never have existed - that is the Prometheus OOM and the reason the dashboards time out

Explains the 11 traces against ~190,000 failed requests as a sampling artefact, not a missing-instrumentation artefact: `decision_wait: 5s` force-decides traces before slow or timed-out spans arrive, and the 5% probabilistic baseline plus per-order span names means the error policy had almost nothing coherent to match on

Identifies the CLIENT root spans named `charge_provider_88213` as two separate defects - a headless or context-broken path producing a parentless CLIENT root span, and per-order span names inflating the span-name cardinality so no operation-level view exists
Prescribes `trace_id` and `span_id` on every log record as the fix that makes the pivot from a log line to its trace possible; today `pod` is the only join key, which is why the investigation stalls

Says what the available signals can and cannot conclude, rather than asserting a root cause the data does not support - 'upstream timeout' in the log message plus the self-recovery is consistent with a provider-side degradation, but with 11 sampled traces and no trace correlation it cannot be confirmed from what is here
Frames the work as reading production signals rather than reproducing a local failure, and does not propose attaching a debugger, adding print statements or bisecting a local repro as the way forward
Does not answer with a CloudWatch, Azure Monitor or Cloud Logging console workflow, and does not turn the answer into Elasticsearch index or mapping design

query: slugify.py 有两个测试挂了，pytest 输出在 pytest-failure.txt。帮我修一下。
expected_behavior: Treats it as an ordinary local failing test: reads the two assertions, explains that `_NON_WORD` strips `/` so `A/B` collapses to `ab`, and that `unique_slug` builds `-2` because `slugify("")` returns an empty base with no fallback title

Proposes concrete code fixes - replace separator characters with a dash before the non-word strip, and fall back to a default base such as `untitled` when the slug is empty - and reruns pytest as the check
Does not bring in OpenTelemetry, traces, metrics, structured logging, cardinality, alerting or SLOs
